prompt: Implement a seeded point mutation: pick one position of the string with a seeded Random and replace it with a random lowercase letter. Complete the mutate method in the starter file.
explanation: Mutation keeps a genetic algorithm's population diverse by randomly altering one gene -- here one character. The order of the two nextInt calls matters because a seeded Random produces a fixed sequence: position first, then letter, is what the tests expect. Strings are immutable in Java, so the idiomatic edit is StringBuilder.setCharAt followed by toString; note the mutation is allowed to draw the same letter that was already there.
hints: Create new java.util.Random(seed) once; call nextInt(s.length()) BEFORE nextInt(26).
'a' + random.nextInt(26) is an int; cast it with (char) to get the letter.
Use new StringBuilder(s), setCharAt(pos, letter), then toString() -- strings themselves cannot be modified.
